messages.subject: median posterior marginals
parts:
Hi,

I would like to extract the medians (transformed) of the model hyperparameters and their associate credible intervals (instead of using the mean given in the summary("results")). How can I do this?

I've tried this:

sqrt((1/(median(results$marginals.hyperpar$`Precision for the Gaussian observations`)))),

but not sure if this is correct, and do not know how to get the associated credible intervals.

I am interested in using the median estimates since the mean may be skewed.

Thank you

Natoya

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] median posterior marginals
parts:
you'll find the median in the output as well,

if you want the median for a transformed variable, then quantiles are just mapped. 
so this is the median for the precision
> inla.qmarginal(0.5, r$marginals.hyperpar[[1]])
[1] 13840.841

and this the median for the variance = 1/prec

> 1/inla.qmarginal(0.5, r$marginals.hyperpar[[1]])
[1] 7.22499449e-05
>


> r=inla(y~1,data=data.frame(y=1))
> summary(r)

mean sd 0.025quant 0.5quant 0.975quant mode kld

(Posterior marginals needs also 'control.compute=list(return.marginals.predictor=TRUE)')

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] median posterior marginals
parts:
The posterior medians are already given in the summary output, in the “0.5quant”. You’ll also find the endpoints of a credible interval via the two quantiles in the adjacent columns.

Finn
